snippet: Climate change affects agriculture through altered rainfall patterns, increased temperatures, and more frequent extreme weather events. Crop yields are projected to decline in many tropical regions. Adaptation strategies include drought-resistant crops, improved irrigation, and shifting planting calendars. Sustainable practices can help mitigate impact while ensuring food security.

Renewable energy in developing countries can reduce dependence on fossil fuels, create local jobs, and improve energy access in remote areas. Solar and wind costs have fallen significantly. Challenges include financing, grid integration, and technical capacity. International support and green bonds are helping scale deployment.

Large language models (LLMs) like ChatGPT are trained on vast text corpora to predict the next token. They can generate coherent text, answer questions, and perform tasks via prompting. Key concepts include transformers, attention mechanisms, and reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF). They are used in chatbots, code assistants, and content generation.

Ethical considerations in AI include bias and fairness, transparency, accountability, privacy, and societal impact. Models can perpetuate biases present in training data. Responsible AI involves diverse data, explainability, human oversight, and clear policies. Regulations such as the EU AI Act aim to set standards for high-risk applications.

Agentic AI refers to systems that plan, use tools, and execute multi-step tasks autonomously. Examples include research agents that search and summarize, coding agents that edit files, and workflow agents that integrate with n8n or Zapier. Key capabilities are tool use, memory, and reasoning (e.g., ReAct). They enable intelligent automation beyond simple chatbots.
